body.title: S013: exact neighborhood concentration and global extremal restriction
body.body:
S013 closes an all-graph extremizer-selection step in the universal critical ASH* programme: exact loss-preserving even concentration under open-neighborhood inclusion, including zero/singleton receivers with the precise small STACK exception. Choosing GLOBAL Q then degree-weight P places heavy piles at minimal open neighborhoods; both extremal maxima restrict exactly to that domain. The residual incomparable-neighborhood inequality remains OPEN separately for STACK and CLEAR.

The session also gives a conditional CLEAR component comparison and private-exit/all-root THREE restrictions, and refutes actual gap-one first-shadow, adjacent CLOSED-neighborhood and threshold/global-Q deletion-independence proof shortcuts. These are auxiliary failures, not ASH* counterexamples. Complete proofs, dependency/hostile audit, primary attribution/equivalence limits and a complete strictly FUTURE S014 handoff are included. No delegation or later-stage work.

An assigned abstract root family demonstrates that root typing/self-root tests alone do not establish a common STACK root; it is expressly not a graph/configuration counterexample. body.title: S005: exact pure-pile clearing, extremal ASH* audit and independently replayed frontiers
body.body:
## S005 — proof, counterexamples to auxiliary claims, and certified finite frontiers

**Headline:** universal intended critical Almost Stacked Hypothesis (ASH*) remains OPEN for stacking and clearing. The printed-form counterexamples remain separately established. No premature phase-gate, novelty, Lean, Palomar, manuscript or author-contact claim.

- Exact pure-pile clearing criterion is proved using an ancestry lower-bound argument and matching equal-level construction, explicitly crediting April Theorem 6.1 and October equation 4.10 for existing ingredients.

commit.message:
S003: close October source gate; certify counterexamples to the printed ASH; critical-form evidence; prepare S004

- Read arXiv:2610.09650v1 in full: Hypothesis 3.2 has the same content as April 9.1; estim reconciled with TreeStack.
- AS-gap reformulation (complete proofs): the printed least-t equality holds iff an almost-stacked
  loser exists at every size n<t<g(G); the critical form ASH* holds iff one exists at g(G)-1.
- Printed ASH is false: stacking on P4 at t=12 (stack=15), clearing on the bull graph at t=12
  (clear=15). Finite certificates are replayed by an independent checker and in CI. Lean and the
  independent cold audit are pending (S004).
- The authors' public atlas code tests the critical form ASH*. ASH* is proved for trees
  (TreeStack + October Thm 5.2) and complete bipartite graphs, computed true on the n<=7 atlas
  and on all n=8 graphs with threshold <=26, and remains open.
- CAM-S003-01 (preregistered; plan hashed): forward/reverse C solvers, Python reverse fixpoint,
  AS memo solver; exact stack(C8)=31; S002 bipartiteness erratum for C8+chord 0-4.
- Phase 1 not advanced; S004 handoff is FUTURE and unexecuted.
